subject.title: feat(agents): per-agent outbound A2A allowlist override

question: Should OpenClaw accept `agents.list[].tools.agentToAgent.allow` now as the per-agent outbound A2A authorization contract, or defer it to the broader session-visibility permission model?
rationale: The PR adds a user-facing config knob and SDK-visible authorization shape for cross-agent session tools, which is a security/product contract decision beyond the mechanical normalization repair.

options.title: Accept narrow outbound override after repair
options.body: Normalize exact allow entries, rebase, and land this focused outbound-only contract while broader session visibility remains separate.

options.title: Defer to broader permission design
options.body: Pause or close this branch and fold per-agent A2A semantics into https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/59149 or https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/48785.

options.title: Redesign receiver-side semantics first
options.body: Ask for an explicit maintainer design covering outbound-only versus bidirectional or `receivesFrom` semantics before accepting any config surface.

recommendation.title: Accept narrow outbound override after repair
recommendation.body: Normalize exact allow entries, rebase, and land this focused outbound-only contract while broader session visibility remains separate.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest feature-history signal across session-tool scoping, config schema, and adjacent A2A policy work.
